hook: Putting vegetables into a cold pan is the fastest way to steam them instead of getting a nice brown sear.
body: Vegetables are mostly water. When they hit a lukewarm pan, that internal moisture slowly leaks out and pools at the bottom, which can end up steaming your food. But if you preheat the pan with oil until it's shimmering, that intense heat flashes off the escaping water instantly. This dry environment is what allows the vegetable's natural sugars to caramelize, giving you a deep, savory sear instead of a mushy, steamed texture.
cta: Heat your pan for two minutes before adding your vegetables to see the difference tonight.
